title: Vitamin Glow Serum
body_html:
Multi-active brightening serum built around 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid — a stable, gentler vitamin C that targets uneven tone, dullness, and hyperpigmentation without the sting of L-Ascorbic Acid. Clean, vegan, fragrance-free.

  • More even, radiant skin tone visible in 3–4 weeks
  • Fades post-inflammatory marks and stubborn hyperpigmentation
  • Gentler than standard vitamin C — well-tolerated by reactive skin
  • AM and PM compatible — use morning, evening, or both

How to use: Apply 3–4 drops to clean skin AM and/or PM before moisturizer; shake well before use and follow with SPF in the morning.

Key ingredients
  • Niacinamide (B3) — evens tone, reduces post-inflammatory marks
  • 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid — stable vitamin C ether; brightens without irritation
  • Tocopheryl Acetate (E) + Panthenol (B5) — antioxidant + barrier support
  • Linoleic Acid & Phospholipids — reinforce the lipid barrier so actives don't over-strip
Who it's for

Moms dealing with hyperpigmentation, post-baby tone changes, or persistent dullness — especially if L-Ascorbic Acid has been too reactive. For a simpler daily antioxidant baseline, the Vitamin C Serum is the cleaner pick.

Free from

No parabens • No sulfates • No synthetic fragrance • No PEGs • No phthalates

Full ingredient list (INCI)

Niacinamide, 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid, Tocopheryl Acetate, Panthenol, Linoleic Acid, Phospholipids

Size & suggested use

1 fl oz (30ml) · Made in USA. External use only; avoid eye area; discontinue if irritation occurs; keep out of reach of children.

faq_json.question: What's the difference between Vitamin Glow Serum and Vitamin C Serum?
faq_json.answer: The short answer: Vitamin C Serum is your daily antioxidant and brightening baseline. Vitamin Glow Serum is a multi-active targeted treatment for more specific concerns. Choose Vitamin C Serum if you want a consistent AM serum that defends against environmental damage, maintains even tone, and delivers reliable day-in, day-out brightening. Choose Vitamin Glow Serum if you're dealing with stubborn hyperpigmentation, uneven skin tone, or dullness that needs a more targeted approach — it combines Niacinamide, 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid, Vitamin E, and Panthenol for a multi-angle brightening effect. The two are also compatible: some people use Vitamin C Serum in the AM and Vitamin Glow Serum in the PM.

faq_json.question: Can I use this with my PDRN Brightening Serum?
faq_json.answer: Yes, and they pair well. Our Vegan PDRN Brightening Serum focuses on barrier support, hydration, and the appearance of fine lines via PDRN and Acetyl Hexapeptide-8. Vitamin Glow Serum brings Niacinamide and stable Vitamin C to target tone and radiance. Apply the PDRN Serum first (lighter, water-based texture absorbs fastest), then Vitamin Glow Serum, then moisturizer. Together they cover hydration, brightening, and barrier conditioning in one routine.

faq_json.question: Is this safe during pregnancy?
faq_json.answer: Niacinamide and stable Vitamin C derivatives are generally considered safe choices during pregnancy compared to retinoids, hydroquinone, or high-dose salicylic acid — none of which are in this formula. That said, we always recommend checking with your OB or midwife before introducing any new skincare active during pregnancy or breastfeeding. They know your individual health picture; we don't.

faq_json.question: How do I layer serums — do I need both Vitamin C Serum and Vitamin Glow Serum?
faq_json.answer: You don't need both, but using them together is a common approach. Vitamin C Serum (triple ascorbic acid + Ferulic Acid) is optimized for the morning routine where antioxidant protection matters most. Vitamin Glow Serum works morning or evening and targets tone and radiance from multiple angles. A practical split: Vitamin C Serum in the AM, Vitamin Glow Serum in the PM. If you're choosing just one: pick Vitamin C Serum for daily antioxidant protection and general brightening, or Vitamin Glow Serum for more targeted work on uneven tone and hyperpigmentation.

faq_json.question: What actives are in this?
faq_json.answer: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3), 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid (a stable Vitamin C ether), Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E), Panthenol (Pro-Vitamin B5), Linoleic Acid, and Phospholipids. No L-Ascorbic Acid — the stable ether derivative is used instead, which means less oxidation risk and generally better tolerance for sensitive skin.

faq_json.question: Will this help with dark spots or hyperpigmentation?
faq_json.answer: Yes — this is one of the most appropriate products in the Leaf & Bird line for that goal. Niacinamide is among the most evidence-backed topical actives for reducing the appearance of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and general discoloration. The stable Vitamin C ether adds additional brightening support. Meaningful results on established dark spots typically emerge at 6–8 weeks of consistent use. Fresh or active marks respond faster.

faq_json.question: How long until I see results?
faq_json.answer: For general radiance and a more even-looking tone, most users notice visible improvement within 3–4 weeks of consistent use. For more established hyperpigmentation or dark spots, allow 6–8 weeks. Niacinamide and stable Vitamin C are cumulative — consistency matters more than any single application. Using morning and evening accelerates results versus once-daily use.
